title: VSEPR shapes
examples: How do lone pairs affect the bond angles?
Can you explain why the shape of ammonia is pyramidal?
What is the difference between electron pair geometry and molecular geometry?

explain.say: Today we are learning about VSEPR theory shapes.

items: VSEPR stands for Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion.
It predicts the geometry of molecules.
Electron pairs repel each other to maximize distance.

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a water molecule. Look at the oxygen atom, the hydrogen atom and the covalent bond. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
The first thing to consider are the total electron pairs.

draw.text: Total Electron Pairs: Count them all

explain.say: Next we look at the bond angles formed by the atoms.
Finally, we must account for the lone pairs on the central atom.

draw.text: Lone Pairs: They take up space

explain.say: Consider water, which has two bonding pairs and two lone pairs.
In ammonia, the nitrogen has three bonding pairs and one lone pair.

faq.q: Does the number of lone pairs change the shape?
faq.a: Yes, lone pairs exert more repulsion than bonding pairs. This extra repulsion compresses the bond angles slightly.
asks: How do lone pairs affect the angle?
Will more lone pairs make it squashed?

faq.q: Is the electron geometry always the same as the molecular geometry?
faq.a: No, they are not always the same. Electron geometry describes all pairs, while molecular geometry only shows the atoms.
asks: What is the difference between electron and molecular shape?
Do I use one or the other?

faq.q: Does the type of atom matter for the shape?
faq.a: Yes, the number of valence electrons determines the total number of electron pairs available.
asks: Does the element change the shape?
Is it only about the atoms attached?

faq.q: What is the ideal bond angle for four groups?
faq.a: The ideal bond angle when there are four electron domains is one hundred ten degrees.
asks: What is the perfect angle for four groups?
Can you tell me the ideal angle for four groups?

faq.q: What is the geometry of methane, CH₄?
faq.a: Methane has four bonding pairs and zero lone pairs, resulting in a tetrahedral shape with angles near one hundred ten degrees.
asks: What is the shape of methane?
How many bonds does methane have?

faq.q: Why is the angle in ammonia less than one hundred ten degrees?
faq.a: Because the single lone pair on the nitrogen atom pushes the three bonding pairs closer together, reducing the bond angle.
asks: Why is the angle smaller in NH₃?
What causes the angle compression in ammonia?

facts: VSEPR theory states that electron pairs repel each other.
The geometry is determined by the total number of electron domains.
Lone pairs cause a greater repulsion than bonding pairs.
Four electron domains result in a tetrahedral electron geometry.

quiz.say: A molecule with three bonding pairs and one lone pair has a geometry of:
quiz.why: The single lone pair on the central atom causes the three bonds to be pushed down, resulting in a pyramidal shape.

wrong.0: This shape only accounts for three electron domains, forgetting the lone pair.
wrong.1: This shape is only for two electron domains, which is incorrect for three bonds.
wrong.3: This shape assumes all four electron domains are equal, ignoring the repulsion from the lone pair.

quiz.say: What is the electron geometry for a molecule like CO₂?
quiz.why: Carbon dioxide has two bonding pairs and no lone pairs, forcing the atoms into a straight line.

wrong.0: This shape requires three electron domains, not just two.
wrong.2: This shape is typically seen when there are lone pairs present.
wrong.3: This term is used for specific arrangements, not the general geometry here.

quiz.say: If a central atom has two bonding pairs and two lone pairs, what is the predicted bond angle?
quiz.why: The two lone pairs exert more repulsion than the two bonding pairs, compressing the bond angle from the ideal one hundred ten degrees.

wrong.0: This angle is associated with three electron domains in a trigonal planar arrangement.
wrong.1: This angle is only seen when the molecule is linear.
wrong.3: This is the ideal angle for four electron domains, ignoring the lone pair effect.
